policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV text reads "from God the Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ", attaching hemon to kyriou (base). The mapped textual_variant note gives the alternative "from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ" (r01) as the margin, so the ASV text renders the base order.

hyper and peri are both rendered "for our sins"; the ASV wording does not distinguish the prepositions and the only notes on the verse are alternative_rendering (age; God and our Father), which cannot decide a reading.

"out of this present evil world" renders either Greek word order identically; English attributive order is fixed and carries no witness to the position of enestotos. No textual_variant note is mapped here.
Present euangelizetai and aorist euangelisetai in this subjunctive clause are both rendered "should preach"; the ASV makes no aspectual distinction and no mapped note addresses it.

ASV text has "should preach unto you any gospel", rendering hymin; the mapped textual_variant note "Some ancient authorities omit unto you" places the omission (r01) in the margin, confirming the text follows the base.
ASV reads "if I were still pleasing men" with no conjunction, while it does render the earlier gar ("For am I now seeking"); the added gar of r01 is unrepresented, so the text follows the base.
ASV opens "For I make known to you, brethren" — "For" renders gar (base); de would give "But/Now". The connective is explicit in the English.

ASV renders the correlative pair "For neither did I receive it from man, nor was I taught it"; "neither ... nor" answers oute ... oute (base), whereas oude would give "not even/nor" without the first correlative member.
ASV reads "when it was the good pleasure of God", with an unitalicized subject God answering ho theos; the base lacks any such subject, so the text includes the addition.
"after three years" renders either order; English fixes numeral before noun and carries no witness to the Greek sequence, and no textual_variant note is mapped here.
ASV names the man "Cephas", transliterating Kephan (base); Petron would be rendered "Peter". The proper name is decisive.
